title: Punjab Police Arrest FBI Most Wanted Fraudster Who Fled U.S. Over $600,000 SNAP Scam
excerpt: Manjeet Singh Bedi, a naturalized American citizen wanted for wire fraud and food benefits theft, was captured in Jalandhar after fleeing the United States through Canada.
body:
• Punjab Police arrested Manjeet Singh Bedi, 65, in Jalandhar — the fifth fugitive captured under the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters initiative in three months.
  • Bedi allegedly defrauded the U.S. government of at least $600,000 by swiping SNAP recipients' EBT cards at his Tacoma, Washington grocery store and pocketing half the cash.
  • After being indicted on wire fraud charges, Bedi violated court orders, drove to Canada, and fled to India in April 2026.
  • The FBI is working with Indian authorities to extradite Bedi back to the United States to face federal charges.

Punjab Police arrested Manjeet Singh Bedi, a 65-year-old naturalized American citizen on the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list, in Jalandhar this week, bringing to five the number of fugitives captured under the bureau's three-month-old initiative targeting major financial criminals.

Bedi was apprehended at Paragpur in connection with a local fraud case registered at the Rama Mandi police station, according to Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh. During questioning, officers discovered his status as a federal fugitive wanted for defrauding the U.S. government of at least $600,000.

The SNAP Benefits Scheme

Federal investigators allege Bedi ran a systematic fraud operation from his small grocery store in Tacoma, Washington, called Asian Grocery Store, between March 2024 and June 2025. Instead of selling food to participants of the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, Bedi allegedly swiped their Electronic Benefit Transfer cards and handed them cash, keeping roughly half of the proceeds for himself.

"This fugitive ran the Asian Grocery Store like a money laundering operation that converted federal food assistance for the needy into a personal cash dispensary to feed his own greed."

— John Walk, USDA Inspector General

"These benefits are intended to help vulnerable individuals make ends meet," said W. Mike Herrington, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Seattle Field Office. The diverted funds, he said, were meant to help low-income residents meet basic nutritional needs.

A Cross-Border Escape

After being indicted on wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud charges, Bedi was permitted to remain out of custody given his lack of prior criminal history. A judge ordered him to surrender his passport and stay within Washington state.

He did neither. Investigators say Bedi drove across the border into Canada and then traveled to India in April 2026. A federal arrest warrant was issued on May 21 by the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington after he was charged with violating conditions of supervision.

The FBI placed Bedi on its Most Wanted Fraudsters list on September 3 and offered a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to his arrest and conviction.

Fifth Capture in Three Months

Bedi's arrest is the fifth under the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters initiative, launched in June to pursue fugitives accused of large-scale financial crimes who have fled overseas.

"Five Most Wanted Fraudsters captured in just three months is a historic success for this initiative. The days of taking advantage of American taxpayers without consequence are over."

— Kash Patel, FBI Director

According to Patel, the five suspects captured so far are collectively accused of more than $2 billion in fraud and had spent nearly 4,000 combined days on the run before their arrests.

"As this arrest in India shows, the Justice Department's reach extends to every corner of the planet," said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division.

Local Charges in India

Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav confirmed that Bedi was traced and arrested by the Jalandhar Commissionerate Police. Beyond the FBI case, Bedi faces separate charges in India — police have booked him under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for cheating and criminal breach of trust, along with provisions of the Punjab Travel Professionals Regulation Act for allegedly duping a person on the pretext of helping them go abroad.

What Happens Next

The FBI said it is actively working to secure Bedi's return to the United States. Indian authorities are examining his activities and contacts in the country while coordinating with U.S. agencies. Extradition proceedings may follow as cases against him advance in both India and the United States.
nri_angle: A naturalized American citizen of Indian origin is caught between two countries' legal systems after allegedly defrauding a U.S. federal food assistance program and fleeing to India.
author: Diaspora Desk
